items.title: Two inmates flee Dengkil drug rehabilitation centre
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two inmates fled the National Anti-Drug Agency's (Nada) Dengkil National Drug Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) in Sepang today. Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the two fled the rehabilitation centre before stealing a vehicle from a nearby village. He said Nada, in cooperation with police, was conducting an extensive operation to track down and arrest the two inmates.

items.title: Family of four found dead in Kepong condominium
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man, his wife and their two children were found dead at a condominium in Desa ParkCity, Kepong, today. It is understood that police were alerted to the incident this afternoon before personnel from the Sentul police headquarters were dispatched to the scene. A police forensic team was at the scene conducting examinations and collecting evidence.

items.title: MetMalaysia DG: Haze likely to persist until National Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The nation will likely still experience hazy weather until the National Day on Aug 31, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) Director-General Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. He said such a forecast was made due to persistent fire hotspots in southern Sumatra and western Kalimantan, coupled with southwesterly winds heading towards Malaysia. "Analysis of weather forecast models monitored by MetMalaysia shows that several areas in Malaysia remain at risk of experiencing hazy weather with reduced visibility from Aug 27 to 31 2026, due to the influence of southwesterly winds and a high number of persistent hotspots in southern Sumatra and western Kalimantan," he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: Soldier killed in crash two days after wedding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Just two days after tying the knot, a 24-year-old soldier was killed in a road crash in Tampin, Negri Sembilan. Soldier Muhammad Alif Ahmad Rozaini succumbed to his injuries yesterday following a collision involving his motorcycle and two cars on Tuesday. The victim's elder sister, Umminadhrah Ahmad Rozaini, 29, said the family was devastated by the sudden loss of the sixth of nine siblings.

items.title: TNB deliver resilient 1h 2026 performance, protecting the rakyat amid west asia volatility
items.summary: TENAGA Nasional Bhd (TNB) maintained a resilient performance in the first half of the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (1H 2026), reaffirming its ability to deliver reliable and secure electricity, strengthening national energy security and advancing Malaysia's energy transition amid a dynamic global energy landscape. Against the backdrop of global energy market volatility, increasing electricity demand and evolving energy transition requirements, TNB remained focused on maintaining operational excellence, supported by disciplined financial management and strategic execution of its integrated business model. TNB President/Chief Executive Officer Datuk Ir Ts Shamsul Ahmad said the group's performance enabled it to continue investing in Malaysia's energy ecosystem while delivering value to its stakeholders.

items.title: Sultan of Pahang orders three-day mourning for elder sister
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, has ordered the Pahang royal family to observe three days of mourning following the death of his elder sister, Tengku Puteri Seri Kemala Tengku Datuk Seri Aishah Almarhum Sultan Ahmad Shah. Comptroller of the Royal Household of the Sultan of Pahang Maj Gen Datuk Mohamed Zahari Yahya said in a statement that the three-day mourning period would begin today and continue until Saturday. "The passing of the late Tengku Puteri is a great loss to the Pahang royal family, particularly to the Sultan of Pahang and Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.

items.title: Fadhlina directs probe over pupil's death after school run
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has instructed the ministry's Integrity Unit to take action following the death of an 11-year-old student after a school run. Fadhlina's call comes as the Kedah Education Department had launched an investigation into a complaint lodged by Nur Qaira Alisha Ahmad Ilwan's family. "I have followed the passing of the late Nur Qaira Alisha Ahmad Ilwan with deep sorrow.

items.title: Nepal floods: No official confirmation of M'sian casualties so far - Wisma Putra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Ministry said it has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties in the devastating flood in Nepal amid unverified information circulating on social media. The ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said it is urgently seeking confirmation from the Nepalese authorities through the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu. "At this stage, the Ministry has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties," the ministry said in its media advisory on Thursday.

items.title: Nepal floods: Embassy tracking M'sians in Kathmandu hospitals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu is in close contact with hospitals in the Nepalese capital to identify if there are Malaysians who have been brought for treatment following the massive floods that hit the country. Charge d'Affaires ad interim of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu Mohd Firdaus Azman said the move was taken following communication constraints with those in the affected areas. "Given that communication constraints with them are currently affected, we are in close contact with hospitals, especially in Kathmandu, to identify if there are Malaysians who have been brought to Kathmandu for treatment," he said in an interview with RTM, today.

items.title: 1,476 Myanmar refugees to be repatriated on Sept 29 – Home Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,476 out of 5,000 Myanmar refugees will be repatriated to their home country on Sept 29 under the first phase of the Voluntary Repatriation Programme implemented by the government through the Home Ministry. The ministry said the individuals had been identified by the Government of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar through Diplomatic Note No. "The Madani Government, through Home Ministry, has finalised the first phase of the voluntary repatriation programme involving 5,000 eligible Myanmar refugees to their home country.

items.title: Former Negri Sembilan PH assemblymen appeal against allocation repayment order
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Former Pakatan Harapan (PH) assemblymen in Negri Sembilan have appealed to the state government to review its order for them to return allocations already spent on welfare and community assistance. He said the allocations were channelled quarterly rather than monthly. he said.

items.title: Families await news of 26 Malaysians missing after Nepal-Tibet floods
items.summary: That was the anxious plea of M Subra, 38, who is awaiting news of his father-in-law, V Krishnan, 74, after contact was lost with a group of 26 Malaysians travelling on a spiritual pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet following severe flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border yesterday. He said the families received the group's last photograph at about 8am yesterday, when they were still waiting to enter Tibet. He said he was also trying to obtain further information from Wisma Putra.

items.title: Myanmar cleaner charged with offering RM1,400 bribe to cop
items.summary: The 41-year-old was accused of giving RM1,400 in cash to a policeman serving at Gua Musang district police station in April 2026. She was charged under Section 16(b)(B) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009. Deputy Public Prosecutor Asmah Che Wan prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Shastidaran Sathaiseelan.

items.title: 'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladic dead
items.summary: BELGRADE: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb military chief dubbed the "Butcher of Bosnia" for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, has died, Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported on Thursday. Mladic, who had suffered several strokes in recent months, was serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity after overseeing the Srebrenica slaughter, Europe's worst act of bloodshed since World War II. The 1992-1995 war left around 100,000 people dead and 2.2 million displaced.

items.title: EP Manufacturing Q2 profit jumps 19-fold on Chinese carmaker partnerships
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: EP Manufacturing Bhd's net profit surged nearly 19-fold to RM5.15 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM277,000 a year earlier, driven by its automotive localisation partnerships with Chinese carmakers. Revenue for the quarter rose to a 10-year high of RM212.68 million from RM127.7 million a year earlier. For the first six months, net profit increased to RM6.7 million from RM1.05 million, while revenue climbed to RM372.87 million from RM253.23 million.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - August 27, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: Here are today's top stories. Ismail Sabri charged Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was charged with failing to comply with an MACC notice to declare his assets. TH officials remanded Two former senior Tabung Haji officials have been remanded for seven days as MACC investigates issues raised in the RCI report.

items.title: National Day 2026 address ceremony moved to PICC due to haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 National Day Prime Address ceremony scheduled for Aug 30 will be moved from Dataran Merdeka to the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) due to the current haze conditions. The National Day and Malaysia Day Celebration Working Committee said the ceremony would proceed at 9.30pm on Aug 30 at PICC as a precautionary measure to ensure the safety, health and comfort of guests and the public. Earlier, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the government would decide whether to adjust the scale and venue of the 2026 National Day celebrations amid deteriorating air quality caused by the haze nationwide.

items.title: Cabinet approves in principle Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Elevated Expressway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today that the Cabinet has approved in principle to the proposed development of the Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Elevated Expressway (BSE). He said in a statement that the decision reflected the MADANI Government's commitment to providing high-impact infrastructure that benefits the people, spur economic growth and enhance the country's competitiveness in a sustainable manner. These include the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, Maju Highway (MEX), Sungai Besi Expressway (Besraya), New Pantai Expressway (NPE), Shah Alam Highway (Kesas) and the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal System (Sprint) highway network.

items.title: Zara inquest: Handwriting on several loose sheets matches Wina's
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Several loose sheets examined in connection with the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir showed similarities with handwriting attributed to a declared writer identified as "Wina", the Coroner's Court heard today. Forensic document examiner Tay Eue Kam said the handwriting on loose sheets marked Y9B, Y10A and Y10B showed similarities with handwriting attributed to the declared writer Wina in an indented impression recovered from page 50i of the olive-green "Love And Peace" journal marked WK9. However, Tay told the court that she did not have an actual specimen handwriting of 'Wina' for comparison.

items.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: Death toll hits 362, more than 1,400 missing
items.summary: Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet's sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash. Nepali police said they had recovered 359 bodies. Beijing said 100 Chinese citizens are missing in Nepal.

items.title: IOI Properties Q4 earnings fall 37pct on lower fair value gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Properties Group Bhd's net profit fell 36.5 per cent to RM523.11 million in the fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM823.93 million a year earlier, mainly due to lower fair value gains on investment properties. For the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), net profit more than doubled to RM2.15 billion from RM1.06 billion, while revenue rose to RM4.44 billion from RM3.06 billion. The property development segment recorded sales of RM3.91 billion, with Malaysian projects contributing RM3.53 billion, or 91 per cent of the total.

items.title: Malaysians urged to limit outdoor activities as haze persists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians are urged to avoid strenuous outdoor activities when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches unhealthy levels, despite improving air quality across the country. Malaysian Environmental Health Practitioners Association chairman Prof Dr Jamal Hisham Hashim said it was too early to determine whether the improvement was temporary. He said limiting outdoor physical activity during periods of unhealthy air quality could help reduce exposure to haze-related pollutants.

items.title: Net profit rises 16.7pct as Sunway delivers broad-based growth in Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Bhd posted a stronger second quarter for financial year 2026 (FY26), with net profit rising 16.7 per cent to RM318.6 million. Its revenue for Q2 increased 13.4 per cent year-on-year to RM2.9 billion. Property development revenue rose 15.2 per cent to RM405 million, while pre-tax profit jumped 57.2 per cent to RM82 million.

items.title: LYC Healthcare external auditor flags going-concern doubts, issues disclaimer
items.summary: In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the healthcare group said its auditor, SBY Partners PLT, had drawn attention to the group's net loss of RM12.69 million and the company's net loss of RM52.49 million for FY26. The group and company also recorded deficits in equity attributable to owners of RM10.62 million and RM4.81 million respectively. The auditor issued a disclaimer of opinion on LYC Healthcare's FY26 financial statements, saying it was unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion.

items.title: Zara inquest: Father, stepsister expected to testify next month
items.summary: The proceedings, which entered their 86th day today, have so far heard testimony from 79 witnesses before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan. The 79th witness, forensic document examiner Tay Eue Kam, completed her testimony today. The inquest, which began on Sept 3, 2025, has heard testimony from various witnesses, including students, teachers, police officers, forensic pathologists, psychiatrists and forensic document examiners.

items.title: Malaysia to repatriate first batch of 1,476 Myanmar nationals on Sept 29
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 27 — The Home Ministry (KDN) has finalised the first phase of a voluntary repatriation programme that will send 5,000 eligible Myanmar refugees back to their home country in stages, the ministry announced in a statement today. The first batch of the Voluntary Repatriation Programme will proceed on September 29, involving 1,476 Myanmar nationals identified by Myanmar's government through a diplomatic note dated August 13. The date was agreed at a coordination meeting involving the Home Ministry, Foreign Ministry, National Security Council and Defence Ministry, after accounting for logistical needs — moved back from Myanmar's original proposal of August 28.

items.title: OCK Q4 profit surges 218pct to RM23.6mil on digital infrastructure boom
items.summary: Revenue rose 24.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM229 million from RM184.4 million, while pre-tax profit surged 135.9 per cent to RM36.1 million from RM15.3 million. Net profit jumped 218.1 per cent to RM23.6 million from RM7.4 million, while profit after tax attributable to minority interests (PATAMI) soared 384.6 per cent to RM19.4 million from RM4 million. PAT grew 19.8 per cent to RM65.1 million, while PATAMI climbed 16.4 per cent to RM46.7 million.

items.title: THMY profit more than doubles on strong E&E demand
items.summary: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), net profit rose 105.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM6.2 million from RM3.0 million previously. Pre-tax profit surged 113.7 per cent to RM7.9 million from RM3.7 million, the company said in a statement. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue grew 17.1 per cent from RM17.3 million, while pre-tax profit rose 12.1 per cent from RM7 million and net profit climbed 39.5 per cent from RM4.5 million.

items.title: Only nine areas records unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Only nine areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at 6pm today. In the Klang Valley, Cheras, Kuala Lumpur registered an API of 155, while Johan Setia in Selangor recorded a reading of 152. Putrajaya recorded an API of 131, Nilai, Negeri Sembilan logged 126, and Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur stood at 115.

items.title: HSS builds momentum on RM2.2bil order book
items.summary: For the six-month period ended June 30, 2026 (1H FY26), the company's pre-tax profit increased 26.6 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM14.9 million, while profit attributable to owners of the company (PATAMI) rose 29.8 per cent to RM10.6 million. Gross profit increased 4.2 per cent YoY to RM33.5 million, while profit from operations grew 32.6 per cent to RM17.2 million. Revenue increased 19.4 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to RM54.9 million, while gross profit rose 27.7 per cent QoQ and pre-tax profit surged 68.7 per cent QoQ to RM9.4 million.

items.title: Nepal embassy in KL appeals for flood relief donations as death toll rises
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Nepal government has accorded high priority to search, rescue, relief and emergency response operations in areas affected by the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River on Wednesday, according to the Embassy of Nepal in Kuala Lumpur. In this regard, the embassy has appealed to Nepali nationals residing in Malaysia, Nepali associations and organisations, businesspersons, social workers and well-wishers of Nepal to provide financial support for those affected by the devastating flood. Financial support can be channelled into the official bank accounts of the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund and the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund at Rastriya Banijya Bank (account numbers: 1130100003762001/ 1130100000006006) and Nepal Bank Limited (account numbers: 00211600510039000003/ 00200100510039000001).

items.title: From outdoors to indoors: Haze forces National Day Eve switch as PM’s address moves from Dataran Merdeka to PICC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The National Day 2026 Prime Minister’s Address scheduled for August 30 will be moved from Dataran Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur to the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) due to the current haze, the Communications Ministry said today. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 9.30pm, according to a media statement issued by the National Day and Malaysia Day Celebration Working Committee. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also expressed hope that the haze would ease in time for the National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.

items.title: Nepal floods: Tok Mat says Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu searching for 55 missing citizens
items.summary: JEDDAH, Aug 27 — Fifty-five Malaysians are reportedly still unaccounted for following major flooding in Nepal, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said, although the figure has yet to be confirmed by Nepalese authorities. He said the information, provided by travel agencies, is being gathered and cross-checked by the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu. Mohamad said Malaysia had deployed additional personnel from Dhaka, Bangladesh, to Kathmandu to assist the Malaysian Embassy in handling the situation by monitoring the operation, managing the welfare of Malaysians, and coordinating with Nepalese security authorities.

items.title: MIC’s Saravanan says he is the ex-minister being charged tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan has confirmed that he will be charged in the Sessions Court here tomorrow. Saravanan, who is also the MIC deputy president, claimed that the initial statement linking his name was made by an individual who just died two months ago, before the individual involved later made a statutory declaration (SD) to withdraw the allegations. Today, a media invitation was issued by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) regarding a former minister to be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest: Handwriting on loose sheets matches mysterious ‘Wina’
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 27 — Several loose sheets examined in connection with the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir showed similarities with handwriting attributed to a declared writer identified as “Wina”, the Coroner’s Court heard today. Forensic document examiner Tay Eue Kam said the handwriting on loose sheets marked Y9B, Y10A and Y10B showed similarities with handwriting attributed to the declared writer Wina in an indented impression recovered from page 50i of the olive-green “Love And Peace” journal marked WK9. However, Tay told the court that she did not have an actual specimen handwriting of ‘Wina’ for comparison.

items.title: 1MDB ex-CEO says he took Jho Low’s word on Petrosaudi deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today that he believed fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho or Jho Low’s information about the proposed US$2.5 billion joint venture (JV) signing ceremony between the company and PetroSaudi International Ltd (PSI) as there had been early communication with the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), in 2009. Shahrol Azral: Yes. Shahrol Azral: Yes.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Witness admits testifying to avoid corruption charges, but denies getting MACC ‘immunity’ deal
items.summary: Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, 54, president of the Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) and managing director of Bumiputera-owned KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, confirmed this as the prosecution’s 27th witness. Azman confirmed that his company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and his relative’s company Addeen Engineering Sdn Bhd had received a total of RM9.35 million from several constructors including RM1 million from Nepturis Sdn Bhd and RM600,000 from Mamfor Sdn Bhd. Azman: Disagree.

items.title: Lubok Antu only Sarawak area with very unhealthy API reading as of 4pm
items.summary: According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Sarawak’s Daily Haze Watch, Lubok Antu recorded an API reading of 210 as of 4pm today, placing it in the very unhealthy category. Four other areas — Samarahan, Sri Aman, Lundu and the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD Serian) monitoring station — recorded unhealthy air quality, with readings ranging from 156 to 158. Samarahan recorded the highest API reading among the four at 158, followed by Sri Aman at 157, while Lundu and IPD Serian each recorded 156.

items.title: Sarawak minister: Dialogue key to resolving issues with Indonesia (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 27 — Sarawak will continue to resolve issues with neighbouring Indonesia through dialogue and engagement rather than allow matters such as the haze to escalate into conflict, said Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. He said the approach was consistent with the spirit of the Malaysia-Indonesia Peace Agreement 1966, which ended the Indonesian Confrontation through dialogue, diplomacy and the willingness of both sides to seek common ground. Abdul Karim said Sarawak had been engaging the Indonesian government over fires in West Kalimantan which had contributed to the haze affecting the state.

items.title: Police find no evidence stress contributed to Hulu Selangor teacher’s death
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 27 — The investigation into the death of a female teacher at a school in Hulu Selangor has so far found no evidence linking stress to the victim’s death. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a detailed investigation, including statements recorded from various parties, such as family members, colleagues and students, found that the victim had been in good condition before the incident. “However, the case is still being investigated as a sudden death report (SDR), and police are working to gather further statements before referring the investigation papers to the Deputy Public Prosecutor, together with recommendations for further action,” he said at a press conference at the Selangor contingent police headquarters (IPK), here, today.

items.title: Shah Alam brawl that killed man linked to secret society turf war, says Selangor police chief
items.summary: Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that initial investigations revealed that both groups operate in and around the state capital and are involved in several business activities. He said police are investigating the business activities and backgrounds of the groups involved in the clash. Shazeli said the incident at Jalan Mandolin 33/5 also injured several people, including three victims still receiving hospital treatment.

items.title: Finance Ministry: No new gambling licences issued under Madani govt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Finance Ministry today described recent remarks by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor on gambling licences in the state as misleading, saying the Madani government has not issued new gambling licences or increased the number of gambling premises. The ministry said Sanusi’s remarks, recently reported by the media, could give the impression that the Madani government was not controlling gambling activities or had approved new licences to increase the number of gambling premises in Kedah. The ministry stressed that the Madani government had never issued any new gambling licences or permits and had not increased the number of new gambling shops.

items.title: Cabinet gives in-principle nod to Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan elevated expressway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Cabinet has given in-principle approval for the proposed development of the Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Elevated Expressway (BSE), Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today. Nanta said BSE, a proposed strategic infrastructure project, could strengthen the transport network and connectivity in Greater Kuala Lumpur by serving as a high-capacity link integrating several major expressways. “These include the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, Maju Expressway (MEX), Besraya Expressway (BESRAYA), New Pantai Expressway (NPE), Shah Alam Expressway (KESAS) and the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal System (SPRINT) network.

items.title: Ismail Sabri out on RM300,000 bail after son settles payment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob left the court complex here today after his son paid the RM300,000 bail imposed on him. Asked about his health, Ismail Sabri replied: “Yes.” Ismail Sabri was then escorted by supporters as he made his way to his vehicle.

items.title: Two Fire and Rescue dept officers among Malaysians uncontactable after Nepal flash floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Two Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) officers are among the Malaysians who remain uncontactable following flash floods in Rasuwa, Nepal. JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said they are its Planning and Research Division deputy director Mohd Sani Harul and Central Region Academy officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa. He said the two officers were part of a group of 10 Malaysians who left for Nepal on Monday night and were travelling to Everest Base Camp (EBC).

items.title: Sunway Lagoon roller coaster accident that landed two in hospital now under Selangor police probe for possible negligence, sabotage
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 27 — Police are conducting a detailed investigation into an accident involving a roller coaster ride at the Sunway Lagoon Theme Park last Saturday to determine whether there were elements of negligence or sabotage. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the investigation was being conducted in collaboration with several other agencies, including the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department and the Selangor Department of Occupational Safety and Health, focusing on technical expertise. Meanwhile, he said police had also recorded statements from several witnesses, including theme park operations staff, ride attendants and the victims involved, to assist in the investigation.

items.title: Dengue cases jump 60.8pc as MOH weighs vaccine rollout due to high cost
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 27 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is still conducting comprehensive studies and evaluations before making the dengue vaccine part of the National Immunisation Programme (NIP), said its minister, Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. Dzulkefly said that the studies also included a cost-benefit analysis, considering that the price of the newly marketed dengue vaccine is still quite high. Dzulkefly said this after officiating the Negeri Sembilan Dental Specialist Centre (PPPNS), an event also attended by the Health deputy director-general (Oral Health) Dr. Zuraida Mohamed, who is also the State Health director Dr. Zuraida Mohamed, here today.

items.title: MACC gets seven-day remand for former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A politician who previously served as Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general have been remanded for seven days to assist in ongoing graft investigations into the pilgrimage fund. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) also obtained a four-day remand extension for a former TH chief executive officer who had already completed an initial seven-day detention period. Both the former TH chairman and the former finance ministry secretary-general, who are in their 60s, were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya at around 4pm on Wednesday.

items.title: King voices concern over Malaysians caught in Nepal floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has urged Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures to assist Malaysians affected by the floods in Rasuwa, Nepal. According to a post on the Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar Facebook page today, His Majesty directed that the latest information on their safety and whereabouts be provided to their respective family members. “I also urge Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures, including providing their family members with the latest information on the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians involved,” he said.

items.title: Safe and sound: Malaysian hikers at Annapurna Base Camp unaffected by Nepal-Tibet floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A group of Malaysian hikers at the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trekking area has been reported safe following a flash flood at the Nepal-Tibet border believed to have been caused by a glacier collapse yesterday. Freelance tour guide Muhammad Hafizal Hamidon said the Malaysian hikers in the area were not affected as the location of the flash flood was far from their trekking route. “The incident occurred in the Langtang Valley, which is quite far from our trekking route to ABC,” he told Bernama Radio when contacted today.

items.title: Penang leaves fate of agency chairman under corruption probe to Putrajaya
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 27 — The Penang government will defer to Putrajaya on the status of a federal agency chairman currently under investigation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) for alleged abuse of power in a land disposal deal. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow also said that the state respects the MACC’s jurisdiction and will allow the agency to conduct its probe without interference. “It is up to the federal government as it is a federal agency, not a state agency,” he added.

items.title: National Day in Putrajaya: 80,000 visitors, nearly 4,000 police, plenty of road closures but 103 shuttle buses to get you there
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A total of 3,811 Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) officers and personnel are fully prepared to ensure security and smooth traffic flow ahead of the 69th National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya. Putrajaya police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said of the total, 2,357 officers and personnel had been deployed for static security and traffic control. Aidi Sham said the main routes and bridges involved in the full closure during the second phase are Seri Wawasan Bridge, Seri Saujana Bridge, Seri Gemilang Bridge, Putra Bridge and Seri Ehsan Bridge.

items.title: Follow the rules when recruiting abroad, tourism minister tells MM2H agents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing has urged MM2H Programme agents to comply with the laws of the countries where they operate when promoting the programme and recruiting participants overseas to prevent confusion and fraud. He said having a licence to operate in Malaysia did not automatically mean MM2H agents had fulfilled the regulatory requirements of other countries. When promoting MM2H and recruiting clients in other countries, they must also understand local laws and cooperate with local authorities,” he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: After ex-PM Ismail Sabri, MACC says ex-minister to be charged with corruption tomorrow
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 27 — A former federal minister is set to be charged in the Sessions Court tomorrow in connection with a corruption-related offence, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) announced today. It is understood that the former minister will be charged under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009, which pertains to the solicitation, receipt, promising, or offering of gratification. Earlier today, former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was charged today with failing to declare his assets under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act, becoming the third Malaysian ex-PM to be criminally charged.

items.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 17 Malaysians on Mount Kailash pilgrimage out of contact, another group led by Everest climber N. Mohanadas safe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Seventeen Malaysians travelling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China, for a pilgrimage have been unreachable for more than 24 hours following devastating flash floods near the Nepal-Tibet border yesterday, raising concerns among their families. She said her family’s last WhatsApp message was received at about 8.40 am Malaysian time yesterday. Meanwhile, Wisma Putra said 55 Malaysians reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu were currently uncontactable following the floods, but it has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties so far.

items.title: Penang keeps close eye on haze situation before final decision on Merdeka parade
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 27 — The Penang state government is closely monitoring daily air quality levels before making a final decision on the upcoming Merdeka parade at the Esplanade. “The minister said yesterday that if the situation worsens, the event could be conducted indoors,” Chow said during a press conference at his Komtar office today. Chow said that if readings hit 200 API or above, the government would likely cancel the proceedings.

items.title: Foul smell leads to discovery of body in aircraft wheel compartment at KLIA2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — An unidentified body was found inside the wheel compartment of an aircraft at Kuala Lumpur International Airport 2 (KLIA2) today. The body, believed to be wearing jeans and a white shirt, was found by engineering staff assigned to open the aircraft’s wheel compartment. However, no identification documents were found on the body.

items.title: CAAM officer killed after RXZ crashes under car in Tawau
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) Tawau air traffic officer died after the Yamaha RXZ he was riding is believed to have skidded and ended up underneath a Toyota Camry at Batu 3, Jalan Apas, in Tawau, Sabah, yesterday. Tawau district police chief Assistant Commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said preliminary investigations found that both vehicles were travelling in the same direction when the incident occurred. He said the 28-year-old local man driving the Toyota Camry was travelling from Kampung Titingan towards Batu Payung, while the victim was riding his motorcycle from Tawau town towards Taman Millenium.

items.title: Marine police officer shot while colleague unloads firearm in Lahad Datu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — A Marine Police Force (PPM) officer was injured after being shot while on duty at the Marine Guard Post in Lahad Datu, Sabah, yesterday. Lahad Datu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Dzulbaharin Ismail said police received a report on the incident on the same day. “The victim received initial treatment at Lahad Datu Hospital before being referred to Tawau Hospital for further treatment.
